passages.text: Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The king of Egypt had a cupbearer and a baker.
These two men served the king of Egypt.
Some time passed after earlier events.
The cupbearer and the baker did something wrong.
They offended their master.
Their master was the king of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָֽטְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was confined.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh had many officers.
Two important officers served Pharaoh.
One officer was the chief cupbearer.
The other officer was the chief baker.
Pharaoh became angry with both officers.
Pharaoh decided to punish them.
Pharaoh put both officers in prison.
The prison belonged to the captain of the guard.
Joseph was also in this prison.
Pharaoh’s officers stayed in the same prison as Joseph.
passages.original: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖ים אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he became their personal attendant. After they had been in custody for some time, both of these men—the Egyptian king’s cupbearer and baker, who were being held in the prison—had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard put Joseph in charge of the cupbearer and the baker.
Joseph served them.
The cupbearer and the baker stayed in prison for many days.
Both men worked for the king of Egypt.
Both men were prisoners in the same prison as Joseph.
One night, both men had a dream.
Each man had his own dream.
Each dream had its own meaning.
passages.original: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ יָמִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃ וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

passages.text: When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were distraught.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in prison with Pharaoh’s chief cupbearer and chief baker.
Joseph came to them in the morning.
He saw them.
They looked upset.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃

passages.text: So he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why are your faces so downcast today?”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in prison.
Pharaoh’s officials were also in prison with Joseph.
Joseph saw these officials.
Joseph noticed their faces looked sad.
Joseph spoke to them.
Joseph asked the officials a question.
He said, “Why do your faces look sad today?”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־ סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: “We both had dreams,” they replied, “but there is no one to interpret them.” Then Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in prison with Pharaoh’s officials.
The officials spoke to Joseph.
They said, “We had a dream.”
They said, “No one can interpret the dream.”
Joseph answered them.
Joseph said, “Interpretations belong to God.”
Joseph said, “Tell me your dreams.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים סַפְּרוּ־ נָ֖א לִֽי׃

passages.text: So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream: “In my dream there was a vine before me, and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes.
passages.sermon:
The chief cupbearer spoke to Joseph.
He told Joseph his dream.
He said, "In my dream, I saw a vine in front of me.
The vine had three branches.
The branches began to bud.
The buds opened into blossoms.
The clusters on the vine became ripe grapes."
passages.original: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־ גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃ וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֙חַת֙ עָלְתָ֣ה נִצָּ֔הּ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ עֲנָבִֽים׃

passages.text: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into his cup, and placed the cup in his hand.”
passages.sermon:
The chief cupbearer spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand.
I took the grapes.
I squeezed the grapes into Pharaoh’s cup.
I placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
passages.original: וְכ֥וֹס פַּרְעֹ֖ה בְּיָדִ֑י וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־ כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three branches are three days.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
Joseph was in prison in Egypt.
Joseph listened to the chief cupbearer’s dream.
Joseph replied to the chief cupbearer.
Joseph said, “This is the meaning of your dream.”
The three branches in your dream are three days.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַשָּׂ֣רִגִ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

passages.text: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you did when you were his cupbearer.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
You are his cupbearer.
In three days, Pharaoh will lift up your head.
He will restore you to your position.
You will serve Pharaoh again.
You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand.
You will do this just as you did before.
You will be his cupbearer again.
passages.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־ כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס־ פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: But when it goes well for you, please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh, that he might bring me out of this prison.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in prison.
\r\nJoseph spoke to the cupbearer.
\r\nJoseph said, “Good things will happen to you soon.
\r\nWhen this happens, please remember me.
\r\nPlease show kindness to me.
\r\nMention me to Pharaoh.
\r\nAsk Pharaoh to bring me out of this prison.”
passages.original: כִּ֧י אִם־ זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְעָשִֽׂיתָ־ נָּ֥א עִמָּדִ֖י חָ֑סֶד וְהִזְכַּרְתַּ֙נִי֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהוֹצֵאתַ֖נִי מִן־ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing for which they should have put me in this dungeon.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to the cupbearer.
Joseph was a Hebrew.
Someone kidnapped Joseph from the land of the Hebrews.
Joseph did not do anything wrong here in Egypt.
They put Joseph in this prison without cause.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ גֻנֹּ֣ב גֻּנַּ֔בְתִּי מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הָעִבְרִ֑ים וְגַם־ פֹּה֙ לֹא־ עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־ שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, “I too had a dream: There were three baskets of white bread on my head.
passages.sermon:
The chief baker was in prison with Joseph.
The chief baker saw that Joseph gave a good interpretation.
The chief baker spoke to Joseph.
The chief baker said, “I also had a dream.
In my dream, I saw three baskets of white bread on my head.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥רְא שַׂר־ הָאֹפִ֖ים כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב פָּתָ֑ר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אַף־ אֲנִי֙ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה סַלֵּ֥י חֹרִ֖י עַל־ רֹאשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
passages.sermon:
The chief baker spoke to Joseph.
He described his dream.
He said there were three baskets on his head.
The top basket held all kinds of baked goods.
A baker made these foods for Pharaoh.
Birds came to the basket.
The birds ate the baked goods from the basket on the chief baker’s head.
passages.original: וּבַסַּ֣ל הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן מִכֹּ֛ל מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹפֶ֑ה וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־ הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew prisoner in Egypt.
Joseph could interpret dreams.
The chief baker told Joseph his dream.
Joseph answered the chief baker.
Joseph said, “This is the meaning of your dream.
The three baskets in your dream mean three days.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

passages.text: Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and hang you on a tree. Then the birds will eat the flesh of your body.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
You are the chief baker.
In three days, Pharaoh will remove your head from your body.
He will hang your body on a tree.
Birds will eat your flesh from your body.
passages.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־ רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־ עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת־ בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials, and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
The third day came.
This day was Pharaoh’s birthday.
Pharaoh held a feast.
He invited all his officials.
Pharaoh called the chief cupbearer.
He also called the chief baker.
Pharaoh brought them before his officials.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ׀ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־ רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his old position.
The chief cupbearer served Pharaoh again.
The chief cupbearer placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
passages.original: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־ שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־ מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had described to them in his interpretation.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew prisoner in Egypt.
Joseph interpreted dreams for Pharaoh’s officials.
Pharaoh hanged the chief baker.
Joseph had said this would happen in his interpretation.
passages.original: וְאֵ֛ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים תָּלָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.
passages.sermon:
The chief cupbearer served Pharaoh.
Joseph had helped the chief cupbearer in prison.
The chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph.
He forgot Joseph completely.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ זָכַ֧ר שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ
